residue_crt — RESIDUE robust op

• Data kinds: matrix × signal → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.residue_crt(residues, periods, weights=None, lo=0.0, hi=None, on_outside='warn') -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import residue; residue.residue_crt(residues, periods, weights=None, lo=0.0, hi=None, on_outside='warn') -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsresidue.get("residue_crt"))

Usage

Weighted robust CRT over real periods -> dict.

Solve v ≡ residues[i] (mod periods[i]) for v in [lo, hi). residues has the band axis first, shape (N,) or (N, ...) — every trailing element is solved independently (one pixel, one sample). weights (same shape, or (N,)) say how much each band is trusted — typically the product of the two amplitudes the phase came from, so a band with no contrast gets no vote.

Method: per sample one band is the *reference* (Wang & Xia 2010, Sec. IV-A, the remainder with the smallest noise variance; the variance of band i is modelled as p_i^2 / w_i, i.e. equal phase noise scaled by the weight, and among equal-variance bands the one whose residue modulo Γ is closest to the common remainder, eq. (55)/(58)). Every candidate v = r_ref + k p_ref inside the range is scored by phasor agreement sum_i w_i cos(2 pi (v - r_i)/p_i) (the maximum-likelihood criterion for von-Mises phase noise); the best one is refined by the inverse-variance-weighted mean of the signed residuals. A candidate carries the reference's own error, so candidates up to Γ/4 outside [lo, hi) are admitted (never so far that one value appears twice). Until 2026-10-15 the longest period was always the reference: with equal phase noise that is the *noisiest* residue in units of v, and in indirect ToF (16/80/120 MHz, σ_φ 0.33 rad) the folding error rate was 0.556 against 0.116 for trying every hypothesis; now it is 0.116 (public raw data, 10 frames: 0.293 -> 0.131, the same as the exhaustive decoder).

Guarantee (Wang & Xia 2010, eq. (47)): write the periods as Γ M_i (Γ their common factor, M_i integers). If every residue error is below Γ/4 the folding integers are exact and |value - v| < Γ/4 whichever band is the reference, because a wrong candidate moves at least one band by a non-zero multiple of Γ, which strictly lowers that band's phasor term (if only zero-weight bands tell two candidates apart, the margin is 0). In phase terms band i may err by 2 pi (Γ/4) / p_i — least on the longest period. A sample whose residues modulo Γ do not fit in an arc shorter than Γ/2 is provably outside that bound (within_bound False; the converse is not guaranteed — an error of a whole Γ is undetectable). on_outside says what happens then: "warn" (default, ResidueBoundWarning), "raise" (ValueError), "nan" (value NaN, margin 0 for those samples) or "flag" (only within_bound). Incommensurate periods (explicit hi) have no Γ and no guarantee: every sample is outside.

Returns {"value", "score", "margin", "residual", "n_candidates", "unambiguous_range", "gamma", "error_bound", "phase_bound_rad", "reference", "within_bound"}: score in [-1, 1] (1 = all bands agree exactly), margin = best minus runner-up score (small = the answer was a near tie — treat as unreliable), residual per band in the units of v; gamma = Γ, error_bound = Γ/4, phase_bound_rad per band, reference = the band index used per sample. hi defaults to lo + the least common multiple of the periods (when they are commensurate); a range wider than that is refused, because two values in it would have identical residues.

Exactness: integer residues of pairwise-coprime integer periods reproduce residue_integer_crt exactly.
